period.label: Item 2 — Month the year ends

validation.how: Every parse and rule message is a plain text line in one 'Needs review' block after Schedule 10 (field keys dropped, first 25 only); no message sits next to its field.

lists.label: Schedule 10 — Reconciliation of Net Income per Books

findings.now: The year is a free-text box that stays editable after the library tile has set it; typing another year and saving stores the draft under that year.
findings.why: Drafts are keyed by (TIN, form, year) and the save upserts over any existing Draft with that key, so an edited year can silently overwrite another year's draft.

options.name: Read-only year from the tile
options.detail: Show the tile's year as a label and open another year only from its own library tile.

options.name: Confirm before re-keying
options.detail: If the typed year differs from the tile's year, block Save and Queue until the user confirms, and never replace an existing Draft row.

findings.now: Schedule 6 always shows four rows and Schedules 8 / 8.1 show four NOLCO rows, with no add or remove control.
findings.why: The official form grows these tables through 'add more' popups (layout counters for Schedules 5, 6, 8 and 10), so a return with more entries cannot be recorded and nothing warns the filer.

options.name: Add / remove row buttons
options.detail: Let the user add rows to Schedule 6 and Schedule 8.1 up to the official maximum and remove unused rows.

options.name: Blocking 'needs more rows' alert
options.detail: When a draft needs more rows than the page offers, block queueing with an explicit message instead of capping silently.

findings.now: Choosing B is allowed, but queueing is then blocked by a custom message; the official attachment alerts are never shown and the page has no attachment inputs.
findings.why: The official exempt and special-rate attachment alerts (for example 'Please provide value on Exempt Attachment Page 1 Schedule A Item 1.') are replaced by text the official form does not use, so filers with several activities cannot finish the return here.

options.name: Disable option B up front
options.detail: Mark B as unsupported in this build before the filer enters the rest of the return.

options.name: Attachment editor
options.detail: Add the Schedule A attachment rows per activity and show the official alerts verbatim.

findings.now: Any non-empty text, such as 'abc', is accepted and the return can be queued.
findings.why: The official page alerts 'You have entered an invalid email address format!' (rule 1702mx-validate-email-format-blur), but this port only checks emptiness and length, and the address is also embedded in the submission filename, so a malformed address travels with the filing.

options.name: Inline format check
options.detail: Check the address as it is typed and show the official alert under the field.

options.name: Block at queue
options.detail: Add the official email-format alert to the Needs review list so Queue stays disabled until it is fixed.

findings.now: Errors appear only in a 'Needs review' block after Schedule 10, the list stops at 25 messages without a count, and Queue for submission is disabled with no message beside it.
findings.why: The filer must scroll past nine schedules to learn why Queue is disabled, and the messages use official references such as 'Page 2 Schedule 1 Item 1A' that do not match the on-screen labels.

options.name: Inline error under each field
options.detail: Show the matching official alert under the field it concerns and outline that field.

options.name: Summary beside the toolbar
options.detail: Show a count and jump links to the Needs review entries next to the Queue button.

findings.field: Amount inputs (Schedules 2 to 10 and Part II)
findings.now: A typed amount with two dots, such as '1.234.567', blocks Save draft; the Needs review line shows only the typed text ('"1.234.567" is not an amount.') with no field name.
findings.why: The filer cannot save other work until they locate the one bad cell by hand, and closing the window at that point loses the edits.

options.name: Name the field
options.detail: Prefix each parse message with the field's on-screen label and outline that input.

options.name: Save with the bad cell flagged
options.detail: Save the draft and keep the raw text as a flagged entry instead of refusing to save.

findings.now: Twelve small month buttons fill a row and are greyed out unless Fiscal or Short period is chosen.
findings.why: Twelve buttons are hard to scan on a phone-width layout and give no clear reason why they are disabled; a combobox is more compact.

options.name: Combobox
options.detail: A single-select combobox showing the current month, disabled with a short hint for Calendar returns.

options.name: Read-only chip
options.detail: Show 'Dec' as a read-only chip for Calendar returns and open the combobox only for Fiscal or Short period.

findings.now: IC 055 — MCIT and 13 other ATCs are shown as 14 chips in one row.
findings.why: The official form has two ATC slots (chkPg1I5ATCR1, and drpPg1I5ATCR2 with chkPg1I5ATCR2), so IC 055 and one other ATC can be picked together, which a single chip row does not show.

options.name: Multi-select combobox
options.detail: A combobox that lets the filer pick IC 055 and one other ATC, listing the selected codes.

options.name: Two controls
options.detail: A checkbox for IC 055 and a single-select combobox for the other ATC, mirroring the two official slots.

findings.field: (outside the form's files: shared XML writer, layout tool, app shell)
findings.now: This page's commits also change shared code outside the form's own files: the number rule in the shared XML writer, the layout generator, and the legacy 1702MX route and agent entries.
findings.why: The branch rule keeps changes outside a form's own files to one-line registrations, and these changes alter behaviour that every form's submit XML and the agent control plane rely on.

options.name: Split the shared change
options.detail: Move the NumberRule and layout-generator changes into their own commit reviewed against every form, and keep the 1702MX commit to its own files.

options.name: Registrations only
options.detail: Replace the rule change with a per-layout setting, and keep the app and agent entries as one-line registrations.

findings.now: On reopen, a stored rate with two decimals, such as 7.25, is redisplayed as 7.2 and then passes validation, so a value the filer never confirmed can be queued.
findings.why: The field is rebuilt with format {:.1} while the rule accepts one decimal only, so the displayed value can differ from the stored one.

options.name: Show the stored text
options.detail: Rebuild the field from the stored raw text instead of re-formatting the number.

options.name: Flag extra decimals
options.detail: Keep the stored value and show the 'Item 4B holds one decimal place.' alert until the filer changes it.
